answer: A stake-bonded reputation registry makes each agent lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, so spinning up thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of deposits — like planting a beacon in a tundra where every newcomer must haul its own fuel. Honest agents earn the deposit back plus a share of fees, the way bees return nectar to the hive, while detected Sybils lose the bond, so the attack's cost scales linearly with the number of fakes instead of staying near zero.
